block_framing: Both BLOCKs are HTTP-reachable at HEAD, unauthenticated, and measured on a live server (src.api.app:app on :8102). They share one root cause: the RED counter is keyed on the raw, URL-decoded request path (backend/src/api/middleware.py:75) and that path is rendered into the Prometheus exposition text unescaped (backend/src/api/platform/routes.py:79). One fix closes both: key on the matched route template, cap the series count, escape label values, and put /metrics behind auth. The two prior security BLOCKs (SEC-001 ReDoS, SEC-002 PII in tracebacks) were independently re-probed and are confirmed fixed.

dependency_audit.gate_effect: downgraded to WARN (SEC2-W12) - not reachable in the deployed artefact; fixes are semver-major
dependency_audit.lockfile_note: .gitignore:45,49 ignore *.lock and package-lock.json repo-wide; git ls-files frontend/ shows no lockfile

findings.title: Never-evicted process-global counter keyed on the raw request path - unauthenticated remote memory exhaustion and response amplification
findings.detail: _request_counts is a module-level Counter keyed on (method, scope['path'], status) using the raw URL-decoded path rather than the matched route template. Every distinct path an anonymous client invents adds a permanent key; nothing evicts, caps or bounds it, and the growth happens in the middleware on every request whether or not /metrics is ever scraped. /metrics then renders one line per key, so the response grows without limit too.
findings.evidence: Live server :8102. 60,000 distinct 300-char paths from ONE keep-alive connection in 11.9s (5,047 req/s, all 404). Server working set 92,268 KB -> 121,156 KB = +28.2 MB retained, ~493 bytes per distinct path, ~142 MB per minute of sustained attack from a single connection. /metrics body reached 45,600,000 bytes / 124,012 series; a ~60-byte unauthenticated GET /metrics therefore returns 45.6 MB (~760,000x amplification). Earlier run: 4,000 paths -> 1,071,316-byte body / 4,008 series.
findings.reachability: HTTP-reachable at HEAD (unauthenticated, no rate limit, no proxy in the declared local verification mode)
findings.refutation_attempted: Looked for an LRU/TTL/maxsize, a route allowlist, auth on /metrics, rate limiting, and a bounding reverse proxy. None exist. reset_request_counters() is test-only. Trailing-slash 307s and 405s are counted too, so strict routing would not bound the key space. Path length and charset are unconstrained. Finding survives.
findings.fix: Key the counter on the matched route template (scope['route'].path) with a single '<unmatched>' fallback and an '<other>' method bucket; hard-cap distinct series (overflow bucket past ~500); require auth for /metrics or bind it to an internal interface.

findings.title: Prometheus label values interpolated from the decoded request path with no escaping - exposition-format injection into the monitoring pipeline
findings.detail: The route label is built as route="{route}" via f-string with no escaping of quote, backslash or newline, and uvicorn supplies the percent-DECODED path. A single anonymous request whose path carries encoded quote and newline bytes closes the label, terminates the line and writes attacker-authored series into the scrape output.
findings.evidence: Live server :8102. One GET to a path containing an encoded quote + newline + a crafted counter line produced, verbatim in GET /metrics: a malformed first line with an unbalanced quote, a fully fabricated series of its own (http_requests_total{method="GET",route="/spoofed",status="200"} 999999), and a stray #-prefixed fragment. Probe assertion 'spoofed metric present as its own line: True'. The JSON log sink for the same request stayed valid (json.dumps escaped it) - the two sinks are separate code paths.
findings.refutation_attempted: Traced the path from uvicorn's scope['path'] through middleware.py:75 into routes.py:79 - no validation, normalisation or escaping at any step; PlainTextResponse does not escape exposition syntax. Checked whether the JSON formatter's escaping covers it - it does not, it is a different sink. Considered whether a scraper would simply ignore it: either the scrape fails to parse (monitoring blackout) or attacker-authored counters are ingested, and this project's runtime-SLO sensor (error_rate_pct/p95_ms) reads this surface, so error-rate breaches can be masked. Finding survives.
findings.fix: Escape label values per the exposition format (backslash, quote, newline) AND stop using free-form input as a label by adopting the matched route template; SEC2-B01's fix removes this vector as a side effect.
violates: OWASP A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

findings.title: GET /metrics is unauthenticated, unthrottled and reflects attacker-controlled content
findings.detail: Even once capped and escaped, /metrics discloses traffic volume, status mix and the internal route inventory to any anonymous client, and echoes attacker-chosen path strings back to whoever scrapes it.
findings.evidence: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8102/metrics -> 200 text/plain with no credential; no auth dependency, allowlist or rate limit exists anywhere in the app.
findings.refutation_attempted: Searched the app factory and router for any auth dependency or middleware - none. No AC requires the endpoint to be public.
findings.fix: Require a bearer/mTLS credential or bind /metrics to a non-public interface; never echo unmatched paths.

findings.title: sanitise_context never scrubs non-string scalars - registered numeric PII egresses verbatim in the error envelope
findings.detail: _scalar returns bool/int untouched and sanitise_context only calls scrub_text inside the isinstance(value, str) branch, so a registered 12-digit Aadhaar or a salary figure placed in AppError.context as an int crosses the wire unredacted. That is precisely the shape this PII takes.
findings.evidence: In-process probe with register_sensitive('123412341234', '875000.00'): pan_str -> [REDACTED], aadhaar_str -> [REDACTED], salary_decimal -> [REDACTED], but aadhaar_int -> 123412341234 and salary_int -> 875000. Structured values (dict/list/tuple/bytes/float/object/None) are correctly dropped.
findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD - no production code raises an AppError carrying PII context; becomes a live PII egress the moment a group B/E story puts a numeric identifier in context
findings.refutation_attempted: Checked whether the 200-char cap or the credential filter catch it (they are string-only), and whether any AppError subclass with PII context exists at HEAD (none - src/types/errors.py has no subclasses). Downgraded from high to medium on reachability alone.
findings.fix: Scrub the stringified form of every scalar, or accept only str and Decimal and force callers to stringify.
violates: project rule: NEVER log or expose full PII

findings.title: _CREDENTIAL_URI misses several common credential shapes, which then egress in the error envelope
findings.detail: The regex requires a non-empty username before the colon, so a URI whose userinfo begins immediately with the colon (the usual Redis/AMQP form) is not detected. Credentials carried as query parameters, ADO/JDBC-style key-value connection strings, scheme-less user:secret@host forms, a URI with a space before the at-sign, an AWS secret-key assignment and a JWT are all missed as well.
findings.evidence: 16-case probe of sanitise_context({'dsn': ...}): 5 shapes matched and were dropped; 11 egressed intact, including the empty-username userinfo form, the ?user=&password= query-string form, the 'Password=...;' key-value form, the scheme-less form, an AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY assignment and a JWT.
findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD (no code puts a DSN in context yet)
findings.refutation_attempted: Confirmed the filter fails closed when it does match (the whole value is dropped, not truncated) and that the 200-char cap drops long values - so this is a gap in one defence-in-depth layer, not the only layer. Kept at medium.
findings.fix: Add key-name-based dropping (password/secret/token/dsn/url), allow an optional username in the userinfo match, and inspect query strings.

findings.title: Context keys are never scrubbed, capped or counted
findings.detail: clean[str(key)] = value applies no scrubbing, no credential check, no length cap to the key, and nothing caps the number of entries - so the key channel bypasses both value-side controls and the envelope size is unbounded.
findings.evidence: Probe: a key containing a PAN, a key containing a full credential URI, and a 5,000-character key all egressed unchanged; sanitise_context with 10,000 entries returned all 10,000.
findings.refutation_attempted: Verified the value-side cap works and fails closed (201-char value dropped, 200-char kept and scrubbed), so the gap is specific to keys and to entry count.
findings.fix: Apply the same scrub/cap to keys, restrict keys to a safe charset, and cap the entry count.

findings.title: Redaction is defeated by any separator outside space/tab/hyphen and by runs of 5 or more - demonstrated leaking a registered PAN at INFO through a real log sink
findings.detail: _SEPARATOR_RUN tolerates 0-4 characters from the class [space, tab, hyphen] between value characters. Any other separator, or a longer run, prevents the match, so a registered value that reaches a log sink in a different formatting is written in full. The character-class allowlist, not the {0,4} bound, is the substantive weakness - and widening the bound would reintroduce SEC-001, so the fix is not a bigger bound.
findings.evidence: Live server :8103, PAN registered via register_sensitive, one INFO line through the configured JSON logger: 'formatted five ways: [REDACTED] | ABCDE-----1234F | ABCDE.1234F | ABCDE\n1234F' - the 5-hyphen, dot-separated and newline-split forms all reached the sink unredacted. In-process matrix for the same value: redacted for exact / 1 hyphen / 4 hyphens / 4-spaces-per-char / lowercase; NOT redacted for 5 hyphens, 6 hyphens, 5 spaces, 5-spaces-per-char, newline, '.', '/', '_', ',', NBSP, zero-width space, '%20', literal backslash-n. Grouped Aadhaar: redacted with single spaces, not with 5 spaces or dots. The specific 5-hyphen gap flagged in the review pack is confirmed reproduced.
findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD - grep shows zero production call sites of register_sensitive/redact_values outside src/api/errors.py's scrub_text use, so no PII is registered or logged yet and an attacker cannot choose the formatting of a value no code handles. Must be closed before any origination story (group B/E) logs applicant data.
findings.refutation_attempted: Checked for a normalisation step before matching (none), for a second redaction layer downstream (none), and for whether the literal-escape branch covers the reformatted cases (it does not - it matches the registered spelling byte-for-byte). Checked reachability at HEAD, which is what holds this at WARN rather than BLOCK.
findings.fix: Match on a normalised projection: strip all non-alphanumerics from both the value and the haystack, match on the normalised text, and map the span back to original offsets. Do not widen the separator run.
violates: project rule: NEVER log full PII at INFO level or above

findings.title: _MIN_REDACTABLE_LENGTH = 6 silently skips short sensitive values, giving callers a false assurance
findings.detail: _scrub continues past any registered value under 6 characters with no warning, metric or exception. Real sub-6-character material in this domain: a 4-5 digit OTP or PIN, a CVV, a card/account last-4, a 5-figure salary, a short given name, a date fragment.
findings.evidence: Probe: '1234', '12345', '999', 'cvv', 'Ravi', '50000' are never redacted; '123456', '500000', '110001' are. register_sensitive accepts the short value without complaint.
findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD (no registration sites in production code)
findings.refutation_attempted: The over-matching rationale in the code comment is sound - a 2-3 character value with tolerant separator runs would redact unrelated text - so the skip itself is defensible. What is not defensible is that it is silent. Kept at medium for that reason rather than dropped.
findings.fix: Keep the skip but surface it: raise or warn once from register_sensitive for values below the threshold, and support short values with an anchored word-boundary literal match instead of the tolerant run.
violates: project rule: NEVER log full PII at INFO level or above

findings.title: lru_cache retains PII-derived compiled patterns, and the raw value as the cache key, for the process lifetime
findings.detail: The module documents registration as request-scoped and the contextvar set is torn down correctly, but _redaction_pattern is memoised on the raw sensitive value. Both the cache key (the plaintext value) and the compiled pattern - whose .pattern string contains the value's characters verbatim - survive the request and every later request, up to 256 entries. Applicant PAN/Aadhaar therefore persist in globally reachable process memory long after the request that handled them, exposed to core/heap dumps, a future debug endpoint, or any in-process error reporter.
findings.evidence: cache_info() after 300 distinct values: hits=0 misses=300 maxsize=256 currsize=256. Compiled pattern source for a registered PAN: 'A[ \t\-]{0,4}B[ \t\-]{0,4}C[ \t\-]{0,4}D...' - characters recoverable in order. Pattern still referenced after the redaction scope was torn down: True.
findings.reachability: NOT remotely reachable at HEAD - no HTTP path reads the cache; impact is retention, not egress
findings.refutation_attempted: Probed the three claims in the vector brief. Unbounded memory: REFUTED, maxsize=256 bounds it. Cross-request leakage of compiled patterns causing wrong redaction: REFUTED, the pattern is a pure function of the value so reuse is semantically safe. Cache-thrash DoS: REFUTED as material - 5,000 lookups over 257 distinct values took 33.5 ms vs 0.8 ms warm (40x relative but only ~6.7 us per recompile). Only the retention claim survives.
findings.fix: Memoise on a salted digest of the value (or on a per-request cache discarded with the scope) so neither the cache key nor the pattern source carries plaintext PII.

findings.title: Inbound X-Request-ID is accepted unvalidated and unbounded, then reflected into the response header and every log line
findings.detail: The header is taken verbatim with no length, charset or format constraint, stamped on the response and written into the request_id field of every structured log line. Any client can also choose the correlation id - colliding with another id, replaying a known one, or seeding audit records with a value of its choosing (repudiation / audit-trail poisoning). Honouring the inbound header is contract-mandated (QA-VM-003); the missing validation is the defect.
findings.evidence: Raw-socket probe: a 40,000-character X-Request-ID was accepted, echoed in full in the response header (echo_len=40014) and written into the JSON access log (longest log line 40,146 bytes; 96,588 bytes of log across four such requests). An 8,000-char value behaved the same.
findings.refutation_attempted: Probed the sharper claims separately and refuted them: CRLF/response splitting and JSON log forgery both fail (see SEC2-I01) - h11 rejects bare CR/LF/NUL/obs-fold with 400 and json.dumps escapes quotes and newlines. The amplification is roughly 1:1 (a 40 KB request produces ~40 KB of log), so this is a validation and audit-integrity issue rather than a DoS. Held at medium.
findings.fix: Accept the inbound value only if it matches something like ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$, otherwise generate one; additionally log a server-generated id alongside the client-supplied one.

findings.title: Interactive API docs and the OpenAPI schema are exposed unauthenticated, and Swagger UI loads third-party CDN scripts without SRI or CSP
findings.detail: FastAPI is constructed with default docs_url/redoc_url/openapi_url and no environment gate, so /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json are public. The served /docs page pulls swagger-ui-bundle.js and swagger-ui.css from a public CDN with no integrity attribute and no CSP, so a CDN compromise executes script on the API origin.
findings.evidence: Live probe: /docs 200 text/html (1,015 bytes), /redoc 200, /openapi.json 200 with the full schema. The /docs HTML references two cdn.jsdelivr.net assets and one external favicon.
findings.refutation_attempted: Group A's schema discloses only /health and /metrics, so present impact is low - but the exposure is structural and will describe the whole origination API by group E, and the CDN script inclusion is live now.
findings.fix: Set docs_url/redoc_url/openapi_url to None unless an explicit Settings flag (default off outside dev) enables them; self-host or SRI-pin the Swagger assets if docs stay on.

findings.title: Host header is reflected into the trailing-slash redirect Location
findings.detail: No TrustedHostMiddleware is installed and redirect_slashes defaults to True, so Starlette builds the redirect URL from the client-supplied Host header.
findings.evidence: GET /health/ with 'Host: evil.example' returned 307 with 'location: http://evil.example/health'. X-Forwarded-Host was correctly ignored; X-Forwarded-Proto was honoured only because the probe came from 127.0.0.1 (uvicorn's default forwarded_allow_ips).
findings.reachability: HTTP-reachable at HEAD, but exploitation needs an intermediary (a path-keyed cache, or a proxy that forwards arbitrary Host) since a victim browser sets Host itself
findings.refutation_attempted: Confirmed no allowed-hosts check exists and that the reflected value is attacker-controlled. Downgraded from high because a browser cannot be induced to send a foreign Host directly; the realistic impact is cache poisoning and redirect abuse via an intermediary.
findings.fix: Add TrustedHostMiddleware(allowed_hosts=...) driven from Settings, and/or FastAPI(redirect_slashes=False).

findings.title: No security response headers on any route
findings.detail: Responses carry only date, server, content-length, content-type and x-request-id. No X-Content-Type-Options, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy or HSTS - while /docs serves HTML with remote scripts and /metrics echoes attacker-controlled text. 'server: uvicorn' also fingerprints the stack.
findings.evidence: Measured response headers on GET /health: {date, server, content-length, content-type, x-request-id}.
findings.refutation_attempted: For a pure JSON API the absence of CSP is low impact on its own; it is the combination with the HTML /docs page and the reflected-content /metrics body that keeps this at medium.
findings.fix: Add a small header middleware in the app factory (nosniff, frame-options DENY, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, a locked CSP), and HSTS once TLS terminates in E15-S2.

findings.title: npm audit reports 1 critical, 1 high and 3 moderate advisories in the new frontend manifest (all dev-only)
findings.detail: vitest <=4.1.10 is critical (GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp arbitrary file read/execute while the Vitest UI server listens; GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9). vite <=6.4.2 is high (GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9 path traversal in optimized-deps .map handling; GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff server.fs.deny bypass on Windows alternate paths; GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3 NTLMv2 hash disclosure via UNC handling on Windows - this project builds on Windows). Moderate: @vitest/mocker, esbuild (dev server accepts cross-origin requests), vite-node.
findings.evidence: npm audit --json metadata: {info:0, low:0, moderate:3, high:1, critical:1, total:5}.
findings.reachability: NOT reachable in the deployed artefact - every affected package is a devDependency, vite build output is static, no Node runtime is served, and the Vitest UI is never started (test script is 'vitest run'). Residual risk is to a developer workstation running npm run dev or vitest --ui.
findings.refutation_attempted: Checked dependency type, the test/build scripts, and whether any affected code path ships. It does not. Fixes are semver-major (vite 7 / vitest 5). Downgraded from BLOCK to WARN on reachability.
findings.fix: Upgrade vite and vitest to the fixed majors next sprint; never expose the dev server or Vitest UI on a routable interface.
violates: OWASP A06 Vulnerable and Outdated Components

findings.title: No lockfile can be committed - .gitignore excludes package-lock.json and *.lock repo-wide
findings.detail: git ls-files frontend/ shows no lockfile and git check-ignore confirms frontend/package-lock.json is ignored by the repo-wide package-lock.json entry; the adjacent *.lock entry does the same for backend/uv.lock. CI and every other machine therefore re-resolve caret ranges with no integrity hashes - non-reproducible builds and an unpinned supply chain. The two rules sit under a 'generated / large files Claude should skip' comment, i.e. a navigation convenience with a supply-chain side effect.
findings.evidence: git check-ignore -v frontend/package-lock.json -> '.gitignore:49:package-lock.json'; the 157 KB local lockfile is untracked. git ls-files frontend/ lists no lockfile.
findings.refutation_attempted: Confirmed the file exists locally (so the risk is the ignore rule, not a missing install) and that no alternative pinning mechanism (npm shrinkwrap, overrides, engines) is present.
findings.fix: Narrow the ignore rules to build output only and commit frontend/package-lock.json and backend/uv.lock; use npm ci in CI.
violates: OWASP A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures

findings.title: Probed and refuted: CRLF response-splitting and JSON log-record forgery via X-Request-ID
findings.detail: Recorded because the control lives in the ASGI server and the stdlib rather than in application code - a different server, a BaseHTTPMiddleware rewrite, or a plain-text log sink would remove it.
findings.evidence: Raw-socket probes: literal CRLF in the value (200, no injected response header - parsed as a separate ignored request header), obs-fold continuation 400, bare LF 400, bare CR 400, NUL 400, high-byte value round-tripped harmlessly. Log-forging: ids containing a quote, a backslash and a full JSON object were escaped by json.dumps; 8,050 of 8,050 captured log lines parsed as valid JSON (0 non-JSON).
findings.refutation_attempted: This IS the refutation record.
findings.fix: No change required; validate the header anyway per SEC2-W08 so the guarantee does not depend on h11's strictness.

findings.title: Redaction cost is linear in the number of registered values, per log line
findings.detail: register_sensitive is additive with no cap and _scrub runs one full regex pass per value per record, so a future bulk endpoint registering thousands of values would make every subsequent log line in that request cost hundreds of milliseconds - a self-inflicted DoS through a legitimate feature.
findings.evidence: Measured on a 2,220-char haystack: ~90 us per registered value per log line, flat per value. 100 values -> 9.1 ms; 1,000 -> 89 ms; 5,000 -> 480 ms per log line.
findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD (no registration sites)
findings.refutation_attempted: Confirmed the per-value cost does not degrade with count (no quadratic term) and that the lru_cache removes recompilation, so this is linear scaling rather than a blowup.
findings.fix: Cap the per-request set and/or build one alternation pattern per request instead of N passes.

findings.title: A logger created after configure_logging that disables propagation bypasses RedactionFilter entirely
findings.detail: _install_redaction_filter_everywhere snapshots logging.root.manager.loggerDict once at startup; coverage for anything else relies on propagation to the root handler. Any library imported later that attaches its own handler and sets propagate=False writes unredacted - the classic case being SQLAlchemy echo in E1-S1, which will log statements carrying applicant data.
findings.evidence: Code path read end to end: the filter is attached to the root handler and to loggers existing at configure time only; uvicorn's own loggers are handled explicitly by name (_JSON_ROUTED_LOGGERS), which is itself evidence that late/ownerless loggers are a known gap.
findings.reachability: NOT reachable at HEAD (group A has no database or third-party logger)
findings.refutation_attempted: Verified that propagation does carry records through the filtered root handler for the normal case, so this is a gap for a specific future shape rather than a present hole.
findings.fix: Filter at emit time (a Handler subclass or logging.setLogRecordFactory) rather than by enumerating loggers at startup.

findings.title: /health discloses the service version unauthenticated and no endpoint is rate-limited
findings.detail: The {status, database, version} shape is contract-mandated, but version plus 'server: uvicorn' gives an anonymous client a build fingerprint, and database: down leaks infrastructure state. No throttling exists anywhere - relevant to SEC2-B01 now and to the login/OTP endpoints arriving later.
findings.evidence: GET /health -> {"status":"ok","database":"unconfigured","version":"0.1.0"} with no credential.
findings.refutation_attempted: The shape is frozen in api-contracts.md, so the finding is about exposure and throttling, not the payload design.
findings.fix: Gate version behind auth or reduce it to a build hash; add edge rate limiting in E15-S2.

findings.title: assert isinstance(...) in the exception handlers vanishes under python -O
findings.detail: With PYTHONOPTIMIZE set, a mis-registered handler raises AttributeError from inside the error path instead of failing the assertion, producing Starlette's plain-text 500 and losing the frozen envelope.
findings.evidence: Three asserts read in the handler bodies; they are the only type guard before attribute access on exc.
findings.refutation_attempted: No deployment currently sets -O (no Dockerfile exists until E15-S2), so this is latent.
findings.fix: Replace with an explicit if-not-isinstance raise, or narrow the handler signatures.

findings.title: Probed and refuted: cross-request leakage of the deliberately un-unwound redaction scope
findings.detail: The middleware leaves request_id_var and the redaction set bound on the failure path by design. Probed for cross-request contamination and found none, because uvicorn runs each request cycle in its own task context. Recorded because the guarantee is a property of the server's per-request context copy, not of this code: a synchronous runner or a shared-context worker would turn it into a cross-request PII leak.
findings.evidence: Live server :8103, same keep-alive connection: a request that registered a PAN + Aadhaar and then raised was followed by /probe/scope, which returned {"registered": [], "request_id": "probe-2"}.
findings.refutation_attempted: This IS the refutation record.
findings.fix: Add a regression test asserting an empty redaction set at the start of every request, so a future server or runner change cannot silently break the assumption.

findings.title: Settings.log_level is unvalidated and reaches setLevel directly
findings.detail: Any TRUELEND_LOG_LEVEL value that is not a known level name raises ValueError during build_fastapi_app() and the process never starts; a value of DEBUG in production would also widen what reaches the log sink ahead of the PII controls above.
findings.evidence: Field declared as a bare str with default 'INFO'; consumed directly by root.setLevel(settings.log_level).
findings.refutation_attempted: Not remotely triggerable; availability impact only for an operator typo, plus the DEBUG-widening concern.
findings.fix: Constrain the field to a Literal of the five level names.

refuted_candidates.claim: SEC-001 catastrophic regex backtracking (ReDoS) in _redaction_pattern/_scrub still exploitable at HEAD
refuted_candidates.probe: 44 timed shapes run in-process: the prior gate's '-'*n+'Z' vs all-hyphen haystack up to n=201; separator-free value vs an 'A----'-repeating haystack (n<=48); near-maximal runs followed by a mismatch; all-'A' haystacks; the literal-escape branch over a 400 KB haystack; alternating 'A-' values with a 200-char dash tail; 5,000-value fan-out
refuted_candidates.result: CONFIRMED FIXED by measurement. Every shape sub-millisecond. Prior-gate shape 0.027-0.123 ms (was 199,326 ms at n=41). Growth linear, not exponential. Structural reason: in the tolerant branch the run matches only separators while every value character is a non-separator, so the partition of any candidate match is unique and there is nothing to backtrack over; a value containing a separator takes the literal branch. Worst case found is the ordinary quadratic scan 'A'*30+'B' vs 'A'*L, which measured LINEAR in L (0.445 ms at 1 KB -> 42.7 ms at 200 KB) and is not attacker-reachable since no HTTP input registers values. No new blowup shape found.

refuted_candidates.claim: SEC-002 PII in an exception message bypasses redaction and is logged at ERROR
refuted_candidates.probe: Live server on :8103 with a route that called register_sensitive(PAN, AADHAAR) and then raised with both values in the message; every resulting log line re-parsed
refuted_candidates.result: CONFIRMED FIXED. Both the middleware's ERROR line and uvicorn.error's line contain [REDACTED], neither raw value, and both carry request_id == 'probe-raise'. The 500 response body was the frozen envelope with an empty context.

refuted_candidates.claim: lru_cache(maxsize=256) on _redaction_pattern permits unbounded memory growth, cache-thrash DoS, or cross-request leakage causing wrong redaction
refuted_candidates.probe: cache_info() after 300 distinct values; 5,000 lookups over 257 vs 10 distinct values; identity and purity of cached patterns
refuted_candidates.result: Refuted on all three counts (bounded at currsize=256; 33.5 ms vs 0.8 ms i.e. ~6.7 us per recompile; pattern is a pure function of the value). Only PII retention survives, as SEC2-W07.

refuted_candidates.claim: CRLF / log injection into the JSON log line, or header injection into the response, via X-Request-ID
refuted_candidates.probe: 9 raw-socket header encodings including literal CRLF, obs-fold, bare LF, bare CR, NUL, high bytes; 8,050 log lines re-parsed as JSON
refuted_candidates.result: Refuted. h11 answers 400 for bare CR/LF/NUL/obs-fold; no injected response header in any case; json.dumps escapes quotes and newlines so 0 of 8,050 log lines were malformed and no record could be forged. Only the unbounded-length/forgeable-value half survives, as SEC2-W08.

refuted_candidates.claim: The middleware's deliberate non-unwinding of the redaction scope leaks PII across requests on a keep-alive connection
refuted_candidates.probe: Live server, same connection: register-then-raise followed by a scope read
refuted_candidates.result: Refuted - registered set empty on the next request (per-request task context).

refuted_candidates.claim: X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Proto can be spoofed by an untrusted client to poison generated URLs

refuted_candidates.result: Mostly refuted - X-Forwarded-Host ignored; X-Forwarded-Proto honoured only because the probe came from 127.0.0.1, uvicorn's default forwarded_allow_ips. Re-test in E15-S2 if the proxy configuration widens. The Host-header reflection that DOES work is filed as SEC2-W10.

refuted_candidates.claim: npm audit critical/high advisories should fail the gate

refuted_candidates.result: Downgraded to SEC2-W12 - all affected packages are devDependencies not reachable in the deployed artefact, and the Vitest UI is never started.

refuted_candidates.result: None. No SQL, shell, filesystem or deserialization sink; no hardcoded credentials (Settings sources everything from TRUELEND_* env vars); no authenticated route exists at HEAD, so auth-bypass and IDOR checks are not applicable and must be re-run when group B adds them.

probed_vectors.how: 44 timed adversarial shapes run in-process against the real _scrub, including the prior gate's shape up to n=201 and a 400 KB haystack
probed_vectors.outcome: clean by measurement - all sub-millisecond, growth linear; no new blowup shape found

probed_vectors.name: lru_cache(maxsize=256) keyed on sensitive values
probed_vectors.how: cache_info after 300 distinct values, thrash vs warm timing over 5,000 lookups, inspection of the cached Pattern.pattern and of referrers after scope teardown
probed_vectors.outcome: thrash/unbounded-memory/cross-request-mixing refuted; PII retention in process-global state confirmed -> SEC2-W07

probed_vectors.name: _MIN_REDACTABLE_LENGTH = 6
probed_vectors.outcome: silent bypass confirmed for 3-5 char values (OTP/PIN/CVV/5-figure salary/short name) -> SEC2-W06

probed_vectors.name: _SEPARATOR_RUN {0,4} formatting bypass
probed_vectors.how: 18-case in-process matrix plus a live INFO log line through the configured JSON logger with the PAN registered
probed_vectors.outcome: 5+ separator gap confirmed unredacted, and the wider class (any separator outside space/tab/hyphen: newline, dot, slash, underscore, comma, NBSP, zero-width, %20) also confirmed, demonstrated reaching a real log sink -> SEC2-W05 (WARN, not BLOCK: no production registration site at HEAD)

probed_vectors.name: X-Request-ID taken verbatim
probed_vectors.how: 9 raw-socket hostile header encodings; 40,000-char value; 8,050 captured log lines re-parsed as JSON; response headers inspected
probed_vectors.outcome: CRLF/response-splitting and JSON log-forging refuted (h11 400s, json.dumps escapes); unbounded length + forgeable/collidable correlation id confirmed -> SEC2-W08

probed_vectors.name: errors.py::sanitise_context bypasses
probed_vectors.how: in-process probes: 13-type scalar matrix with values registered as sensitive, 16 credential-string shapes, the 200-char cap boundary at 199/200/201/5000, key channel and entry count
probed_vectors.outcome: int/bool skip of scrub_text confirmed (registered 12-digit Aadhaar egresses whole) -> SEC2-W02; 11 of 16 credential shapes missed, including the empty-username userinfo form and query-string credentials -> SEC2-W03; keys unscrubbed/uncapped and entry count unbounded -> SEC2-W04; the 200-char cap itself fails closed (drops) and the Decimal path IS scrubbed

probed_vectors.name: platform/routes.py /metrics
probed_vectors.how: live server: unauthenticated GET; 4,000 then 60,000 distinct-path floods from one keep-alive connection with working-set sampling of the server process; encoded-quote/newline path injection; arbitrary method tokens
probed_vectors.outcome: TWO BLOCKS - unbounded never-evicted cardinality (+28.2 MB retained for 60,000 paths, ~493 B/path, ~142 MB/min, /metrics body 45.6 MB / 124,012 series) -> SEC2-B01; unescaped exposition-format injection with a fully fabricated series line -> SEC2-B02; plus unauthenticated exposure -> SEC2-W01

probed_vectors.name: frontend/package.json advisories and lockfile
probed_vectors.how: npm audit --json parsed by severity and dependency type; git ls-files and git check-ignore on the lockfile
probed_vectors.outcome: 1 critical / 1 high / 3 moderate, all devDependencies -> SEC2-W12 (downgraded with rationale); no lockfile committable because .gitignore excludes package-lock.json and *.lock repo-wide -> SEC2-W13

not_probed_vectors.reason: Probed single-worker uvicorn only. Under multiple workers each process holds its own counter and cache, which changes the SEC2-B01 arithmetic per worker but not the conclusion; I did not measure it.

not_probed_vectors.reason: No frontend application shell, router or network call exists yet - only money.ts and MoneyText.tsx, both read and grepped for raw-HTML sinks. Nothing to exercise at runtime.

method: Bounded re-verification, instance 2 of 3, reached independently. Read: specs/reviews/review-context-pack.md, git diff 14e9487..HEAD -- backend frontend, all 12 changed production source files plus the changed test files, .gitignore, .claude/claude-security-guidance.md, .claude/skills/gate/references/security-python.md and security-react-typescript.md scope. No prior verdict file used as authority; .claude/state/uvicorn.log not read. EXECUTION, not inspection: (a) in-process timing of _scrub/_redaction_pattern over 44 adversarial shapes and of sanitise_context over 13 scalar types, 16 credential shapes and the cap boundary; (b) a live server (uv run uvicorn src.api.app:app --port 8102) driven with raw sockets for 9 hostile X-Request-ID encodings, with keep-alive http.client for 4,000 then 60,000 distinct-path floods, an encoded-quote/newline metrics-injection payload, arbitrary method tokens, docs/schema exposure and a Host-header redirect check, with the server process working set sampled via tasklist; (c) a second live server on :8103 wrapping build_fastapi_app() with throwaway routes to re-test SEC-002 (register PII then raise) and cross-request scope leakage, with all 13 resulting log lines re-parsed as JSON; (d) npm audit --json plus git check-ignore for the lockfile. Every candidate BLOCK was put through find-then-refute; the two that survived are quantified above and both were reproduced more than once. Probe scripts were run from .claude/state/sec-probe-i2/ and deleted after the run; no product file was modified.
